item.title: One Button From Thought to Note
item.description:
In the previous post I described how I ended up with a speech-to-text service that understands my mixture of Slovak and English, and how little it costs when you pay for it directly. This post is the practical half: how I use it on the Mac, and what I built for the phone over one weekend.

On the Mac: hold a key
#

There is not much to say, which is the point. I hold the right Command key and speak. When I let go, the text is where the cursor was. The audio goes to Soniox as I speak and the words come back while I am still talking.

item.title: How My Health Data Flows Into My Notes
item.description: In the post about Obsidian and Claude I said that the health-data flow deserves a post of its own, and the last part of the series promised it again. Here it is: how numbers from the watch on my wrist and the app on my phone end up in my notes every morning, without me touching anything. The reason it has to be every morning is Feri, my LLM coach: he prescribes the next session from that morning’s data, and he is only as good as what he is given.
